Crossposting a post to other repositories

crossposting-a-post.Rmd
library(blogscapes)

Once a post exists as a folder (its own index.qmd plus any images it references – see the vignette("writing-a-post-from-google-doc") vignette for how to produce one from a Google Doc), crossposting it to other Openscapes-affiliated repositories is a three-step pipeline: verify its images are self-contained, copy the folder into one or more destination repos, then open a pull request in each.

Step 1: verify the post’s images 

verify_post_images("website-new/blog/2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026")

This scans the post’s .qmd for every image reference – the YAML image: field and body ![]() figures – and checks that each one resolves to a file that actually exists inside the post’s own folder. crosspost_blog() copies the folder as-is, so a reference pointing outside of it (or to a missing file) would silently produce a broken image in the destination repo. verify_post_images() errors with the specific offending reference(s) instead.

crosspost_blog() calls this automatically before copying, so running it by hand first is optional – useful if you want to check a post without copying it anywhere yet.

Step 2: copy the post into destination repos 

targets <- crosspost_blog(
  post = "website-new/blog/2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026",
  root = "~/Documents/repos/github/openscapes/crossposting",
  destinations = c(
    nasa = "NASA-Openscapes.github.io/news",
    nmfs = "nmfs-openscapes.github.io/blog"
  )
)

destinations is a named vector of target directories – one per destination repo – that the post folder gets copied into, keeping its original folder name. Relative entries (like the two above) are resolved against root, a common parent folder all the repos live under as siblings; a destination can also be given as an absolute path if it’s cloned somewhere else entirely:

crosspost_blog(
  post = "website-new/blog/2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026",
  root = "~/Documents/repos/github/openscapes/crossposting",
  destinations = c(
    nasa = "NASA-Openscapes.github.io/news",
    nmfs = "/some/other/place/nmfs-openscapes.github.io/blog"
  )
)

By default, crosspost_blog() errors if a destination already has a folder for this post, to avoid silently clobbering an existing crosspost. Pass overwrite = TRUE to replace it instead.

The return value, targets, is the vector of full paths the post was copied to – you’ll pass this straight into Step 3.

Step 3: open a pull request in each destination repo 

open_crosspost_prs(targets, branch = "crosspost-2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026")

For each path in targets, this creates a branch, commits the copied post, pushes it, and opens a pull request via the GitHub API (using the gh package, so it relies on your existing GitHub CLI authentication). It prints the opened PR’s URL for each repo as it goes, and returns all of them (invisibly) as a character vector.

base (default "main") and remote (default "origin") can be overridden if a destination repo uses a different base branch or remote name.

Putting it together 

post <- "website-new/blog/2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026"

targets <- crosspost_blog(
  post = post,
  root = "~/Documents/repos/github/openscapes/crossposting",
  destinations = c(
    nasa = "NASA-Openscapes.github.io/news",
    nmfs = "nmfs-openscapes.github.io/blog"
  )
)

open_crosspost_prs(targets, branch = "crosspost-2026-09-09-openscapes_esip_summer_2026")
